subject.title: fix(message): ignore populated location on text sends

question: Should the shared `message` action continue rejecting mixed location-plus-content payloads, or should OpenClaw define and document a new precedence rule that intentionally drops location data?
rationale: The current public contract rejects the combination, while this PR changes it for every adapter and can silently discard an explicit user-visible location or venue request. The live proof establishes the delivery problem but cannot choose the permanent API semantics.

options.title: Preserve rejection and fix the producer
options.body: Keep the shared location-only invariant and narrow the repair to the generator or normalization path that incorrectly emits a location for an ordinary text or media reply.

options.title: Adopt explicit precedence semantics
options.body: Accept text/media/presentation as higher priority only with a documented public contract, cross-channel behavior review, and tests proving users are warned or otherwise protected from unexpected location loss.

recommendation.title: Preserve rejection and fix the producer
recommendation.body: Keep the shared location-only invariant and narrow the repair to the generator or normalization path that incorrectly emits a location for an ordinary text or media reply.
